atoms.b: Great Britain refers to the largest island in the British Isles. It includes three countries: England, Scotland and ((++Wales Ireland Northern_Ireland)) and is a ((++geographical political abstract)) term, not a political state.

The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland is a sovereign country, thus a ((++political geographical climatic)) entity. Today, it includes all of Great Britain plus ((++Northern_Ireland Ireland Wales)).
Regardless, the terms (Great) Britain and UK are often used interchangeably to refer to the United Kingdom.

Typical notions associated with British culture are ((++politeness rudeness carelessness)), a particular type of humour and a reserved ((++attitude existence country)). At the same time, the term “Britishness” is often understood as a synonym for “((++Englishness Scottishness Irishness))” and is thus ((++incomplete correct favoured)) and controversial. The United Kingdom is often reduced to England, even though the nations of Scotland, Northern ((++Ireland England Isle_of_Man)) and Wales have just as many ((++traditions people land)) and historical roots.
Additionally, stereotypes and the use of “Britishness” often serve ((++nationalistic local global)) purposes, attempting to spread the concept of Great Britain as ethically ((++homogenous diverse complex)), White, and English-speaking. In reality, Irish, Welsh and Scottish heritage as well as more recent immigration prove this picture ((++wrong right neutral)). Yet, ethnically uniform stereotypes of Britishness persist, even though some claim it is an inclusive umbrella term for ((++multicultural uniform united)) Britain.
